name: flowmap.gl
category: A9. Adjacent resources mentioned during discovery
role: deck.gl layer for origin-destination flow maps: sized nodes, tapered or animated flow lines
summary: FlowmapLayer (@flowmap.gl/layers) turns a locations table and an origin-destination flows table into a deck.gl layer with sized nodes, tapered, curved or animated straight lines, and optional clustering. Its strength is migration, trade and logistics flows without hand-built arcs. The animated mode reads the wall clock, so a scene must supply its own clock from t.
use_when: Origin-destination flows between named places, over deck.gl ArcLayer when width and node totals should follow the data
Migration, trade or logistics map scenes inside an existing deck.gl scene
Moving flow dashes captured frame by frame, with Date.now driven from t
avoid_when: Flows that are few and hand-placed: d3 or svg paths are simpler
Scenes without deck.gl: it is a layer, not a standalone renderer
Anything needing its animation on a real clock without overriding Date.now
notes: 2026-11-27: peer ranges let pnpm resolve luma.gl 9.4.0 beside deck.gl's 9.4.2, which breaks the circle shader; pin all @luma.gl packages to one version.

assessment.rationale: Apache-2.0, 9.5.0 published 2026-11-14 on deck.gl 9.4. Gap against deck-gl: no aggregating flow layer. Animated mode reads Date.now in draw, solved by overriding it; niche, so retained as a candidate rather than promoted.

evidence.result: FlowmapLayer animated-straight on deck.gl 9.4.1 MapView (luma 9.4.2), Date.now driven from t, Node 22.19.0 Chromium via @vcr/capture: 90 frames 960x540, 90 distinct hashes, shuffled equals sequential; frames inspected.
evidence.scope: 8 nodes, 12 flows, animated-straight, Date.now replaced by t, no basemap, SwiftShader WebGL on macOS arm64; not clustering, labels, curved mode, picking or other GPUs.
